 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE BHARGAV D. KARIA  Date : 11/07/2023  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

By way of this First Appeal, the appellant seeks to challenge the judgment and order dated 13.01.1986 passed by Extra Assistant Judge, Mehsana, in Land Acquisition Reference NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/889/1986 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/07/2023 undefined No.29/1982, whereby, the reference was partly allowed and the claimants were awarded additional amount of compensation of Rs.2,42,119.60 with proportionate cost and interest @ 9 % p.a. from 23.02.1981 till the amount to be paid.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Reference NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/889/1986 JUDGMENT
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: If the amount is not paid within one year, then interest to be paid @ 15 % p.a. for the period after expiry of one year.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the respondents - original claimants were residents of village Vadnagar, Taluka Kheralu, Dist. Mehsana and were having agricultural land bearing Survey No.2818 and doing agricultural activities.
The said land was in the names of Patel Ranchhodbhai Jivram and Patel Shambhuram Jivram.

The aforesaid land was acquired for the purpose of construction of quarters of Gujarat Electricity Board and Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) was published on 04.12.1980 in the Government Gazette and Notification under Section 6 of the Act was published on 06.08.1981 in the Government Gazette.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer passed an award under Section 11 of the Act on 11.01.1982 awarding Rs.12,321.40 towards compensation of acquired land.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/889/1986 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/07/2023 undefined 3.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants preferred Land Acquisition Reference No.29/1982 before the court of learned Extra Assistant Judge, Mehsana under Section 18 of the Act.

The learned Judge after considering the oral and documentary evidence came to the conclusion that the amount of compensation awarded was less and inadequate and further held that the reference was within a period of limitation under Section 12 (2) of the Act.

4. So far as the issue of limitation was concerned, it was held by the learned Judge that considering the documents at Exhs:46 and 47, it was clear that the claimants were not furnished with the copy of the award and as per the document at Exh:48, it was clear that no certified copy of the award was provided in spite of repeated reminders and it was, therefore, held that when the claimants came to know about the reference, the same was filed.
The claimants received certified copy of the award on 26.06.1982 and reference was filed within the prescribed period of limitation.

5. So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the learned Judge after considering the situation of the land in question near the S.T. Bus Station and there was also a factory NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/889/1986 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/07/2023 undefined situated nearby Shiv Theatre, housing society for Dharoi dam, ganj bazaar etc, it was held that the land was situated in a Executive Engineer vs Patel Ranchhodlal Jivram (Thr'Gh His ...

2 populated area.

The learned Judge has also considered the sale instances produced on record by the claimants of nearby lands and came to the conclusion that on perusal of the document at Exh:29,
land sold was from inside of the town and therefore, it can only be held that the prices were increasing every year.

Reliance was placed at Exhs:25 and 26 to decide the price of the land in question, but considering the fact that sale instance of non-agriculture purpose for housing society and commercial purposes and considering the fact that acquired land suitable for the housing society and commercial purpose

, the learned Judge fixed the price at Rs.18.00 per sq.mtr., resulting into additional compensation of Rs.2,42,119.60 instead of Rs.1.19 per sq.mtr. fixed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
6. Learned advocate Mr. Viral Dave for the appellant submitted that the learned Judge has erred in law and holding that the reference was filed within the prescribed period of limitation as the claimants were aware about the award passed under Section 11 of the Act, inasmuch as possession of the land was also handed over on 23.02.1981 after passing of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/889/1986 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/07/2023 undefined award under Section 11 of the Act and Assistant Collector has also issued notice on the date of publication of award on 11.01.1982.

It was,
therefore, submitted that the reference ought to have been filed within a period of 60 days i.e. on or before 11.03.1982, whereas, the reference was filed under section 18 of the Act on 06.07.1982 and admittedly, the reference was filed beyond the prescribed period of limitation under Section 18 (2)
of the Act.

It was further submitted that the learned Judge has considered the price of non-agricultural land to award the compensation for agricultural land and as such, the impugned award is liable to be quashed and set aside.

7. On the other hand, learned advocate Mr. B.G.Patel for the original claimants - respondents herein submitted that the learned Judge has passed the impugned award after considering the oral as well as documentary evidence on record, more particularly, the sale instances of nearby land.
It was submitted that the claimants produced comparable instances of sale and it is not in dispute that the land in question is situated in a residential area suitable for residential housing colony.

It was further submitted that the land was NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/889/1986 JUDGMENT DATED:
11/07/2023 undefined acquired for construction of residential quarters of Gujarat Electricity Board and therefore, no interference is required to be made in the impugned award passed by the learned Court below.
8.

Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and having considered the oral as well as documentary evidence on record, it appears that it is not in dispute that certified copy of the award was never provided along with the notice dated 11.01.1982 issued by the Assistant Collector and therefore, as per settled legal position, when the claimants is issued a certified copy, period of limitation would start under Section 18 (2) of the Act and therefore, the learned Judge below has rightly arrived at a conclusion that the reference was filed within the prescribed period of limitation.
9.

So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, learned Judge after considering the evidence on record has held that the price prevailing on the date of pre-Notification dated 31.07.1980 as per Exhs:25 and 26 and considering the potentiality of the land being used for the housing society and commercial purpose as per oral evidence of the claimants, has arrived at a Executive Engineer vs Patel Ranchhodlal Jivram (Thr'Gh His ... on 11 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55913448/
3 reasonable rate of Rs.18.00 per sq.mtr.

The NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/889/1986 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/07/2023 undefined learned Judge has also taken into consideration the document at Exh:28, wherein, land was sold at Rs.14.00 per sq.mtr., in the year 1982 and as per the document at Exh:29, the land was sold at Rs.136.25 sq.mtr., in the year 1983 showing the rising trend of price in Vadnagar town.
Considering the said evidences on record, the learned Judge has rightly fixed the price at Rs.18.00 per sq.mtr. which does not warrant any interference.
10. In view of the foregoing reasons, present appeal is required to be dismissed and is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.
